description: Tamil artifact register for the Open Sangam scholar reader. Every record is readable even when its inscription/manuscript layers are not yet digitised: layers carry an explicit status so the reader never invents text or translations. Rights are recorded per source.

classes.description: Stone, cave, temple and copper-plate inscriptions; hero stones and estampages.
Punch-marked, Roman, Pandya, Chola and later Tamil coins and hoards.
Palm-leaf and paper manuscripts, printed editions, lexicons and colonial documents.
Hero stones, bronzes, terracottas and religious icons.
Megaliths, temples, forts and architectural fragments.
Yazh, pann, musical inscriptions and performance objects.
Pottery, beads, tools and everyday objects from excavated Tamil sites.

artifacts.holder: Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology
artifacts.summary: One of the earliest dated Tamil-Brahmi cave inscriptions, associated with Jain ascetics and the Pandya chief Nedunjeliyan. A foundational object for the history of Tamil writing.

text.note: Transcription pending rights-cleared estampage or field collation.

transliteration.note: Transliteration follows the scholarly edition chosen for transcription.

translation.note: English rendering will be cited to a named published reading.

entries: Compare with the Jambai and Arikamedu inscriptions for early Tamil-Brahmi letter forms.
Do not treat this reader as an epigraphic edition until a named estampage and edition are attached.

provenance.value: Catalogued from public archaeological metadata; no image or estampage is reproduced.

artifacts.holder: Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology
artifacts.summary: A celebrated early Tamil-Brahmi inscription associated with a Chola chief and the hero-stone tradition; important for the transition from cave labels to public memorial inscriptions.

text.note: Transcription pending a rights-cleared published estampage.

entries: Useful classroom comparison with Mangulam for script development and royal patronage.

provenance.value: Public archaeological metadata; image rights not cleared.

artifacts.subclass: memorial stone with inscription and relief
artifacts.holder: various district museums and field sites
artifacts.summary: Memorial stones for warriors, sati stones and cattle-raid deaths. They combine a relief panel, a short inscription and a local performance tradition.

text.note: Collection-level record; item-level transcriptions need field documentation.

entries: Reader template supports one inscription per hero stone plus a relief description layer.
Record donor, village, date and reading in the citation, not in free text.

provenance.value: Collection-level metadata; per-object rights review required.

artifacts.summary: Land-grant charters recording donations, boundaries, immunities and royal genealogy. A key source for medieval Tamil legal and agrarian history.

text.note: Requires a specific plate set and a published edition.

entries: Model charter layers: obverse/reverse transcription, boundary list, donor/recipient, date and imprecation formula.

provenance.value: Representative class record; no specific plate is claimed.

artifacts.summary: Chola-period temple inscriptions record endowments, officials, dancers, musicians and temple economy. The Thanjavur corpus is a cornerstone of Tamil epigraphy.

text.note: Attach a specific numbered inscription from South Indian Inscriptions before transcription.

entries: Cross-link with the Chola bronze and temple architecture records.
Cite South Indian Inscriptions volume and inscription number.

provenance.value: ASI public report metadata; inscription image not reproduced.

artifacts.summary: Punch-marked coins circulated in the Tamil country before and during the Sangam period. Symbols, weight standards and hoard context are the primary evidence.

text.note: Legend transcription only when a named coin type is attached.

entries: Reader should support obverse/reverse image layers and symbol glossary.
Record weight, die axis and hoard provenance.

provenance.value: Class-level record; no specific coin image is reproduced.

artifacts.summary: Roman coins from Arikamedu and other Tamil coast sites document Indian Ocean trade with the Mediterranean. They are essential context for Sangam-era ports and Yavana merchants.

text.note: Attach a specific RIC/coin type before legend transcription.

entries: Link to Sangam references to Yavana traders and to the Arikamedu material-culture records.

provenance.value: Public excavation metadata; coin images not reproduced.

artifacts.summary: Pandya and Chola coins carry dynastic emblems, titles and occasional Tamil legends. They support the study of royal authority, trade and temple donation.

text.note: Legend layer requires a specific coin type and published catalogue number.

entries: Reader supports obverse/reverse, weight, metal and provenance fields.

provenance.value: Class-level record; per-coin rights review required.

artifacts.holder: Tamil Nadu Government Oriental Manuscripts Library / Sarasvati Mahal Library
artifacts.summary: Palm-leaf manuscripts preserve literature, grammar, medicine, astronomy and ritual. The reader needs folio navigation, zoom, transcription and a separate note layer.

text.note: Attach a specific shelfmark and folio before transcription.

entries: Model layers: folio image, transcription, transliteration, modern Tamil, English, notes, provenance.
Do not OCR palm leaves without a folio-level correction pass.

provenance.value: Collection-level record; no manuscript image is reproduced.

artifacts.summary: A representative manuscript reader using Tirukkural 1, a public-domain text, so scholars can test the compact multi-layer manuscript view before a physical shelfmark is attached.

value: As ‘A’ is the first of all letters, so the Primal Deity is first in the world.
translation.source: G. U. Pope et al., 1886 (public domain)

entries.gloss: the letter A; the first letter

entries: This is a representative reader, not a claim about a specific physical manuscript.
Replace the surrogate layers with folio images and shelfmark before scholarly citation.

provenance.value: Text and translation from public-domain Project Madurai editions; manuscript object pending.

artifacts.summary: The Tamil Lexicon is the foundational historical dictionary of Tamil. It is public domain and an ideal first document-reader for headword, etymology and citation layers.

text.note: Attach a specific headword and volume/page.

value: Lexicon entries are already bilingual Tamil–English; the reader can display the headword, Tamil definition and English gloss as separate layers.

entries: Use this record as the first document/lexicon ingest target.
Cite volume and page for every extracted entry.

provenance.value: Public-domain edition; verify the Internet Archive item is the public-domain scan.

artifacts.holder: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (open-access example)
artifacts.summary: Chola bronzes are among the great achievements of Tamil sculpture. The Nataraja icon fuses dance, cosmology and Saiva theology; object metadata can be linked to Tamil literary and ritual texts.

text.note: Iconographic labels and associated Tamil hymns can be attached as a text layer.

entries: Use a Met CC0 object record before attaching an image.
Distinguish the iconography layer from any specific temple provenance.

provenance.value: Class record; attach a specific Met object ID and CC0 citation before publishing an image.

artifacts.summary: Terracottas from Arikamedu show everyday dress, ornament and ritual life in an Indo-Roman trading port. They complement the Roman coin and pottery records.

text.note: Object labels and excavation context form the text layer.

entries: Attach excavation report, context, and museum accession number.

provenance.value: Excavation metadata; image rights per museum.

artifacts.holder: Archaeological Survey of India / state protected sites
artifacts.summary: Megalithic dolmens, cists and urn burials are the material background of early Tamil society. They connect archaeology with Sangam references to memorial and burial practices.

text.note: Site plan, typology and excavation notes form the text layer.

entries: Use site-level protection status and ASI/state inventory number.

provenance.value: Public site metadata; no site image reproduced.

artifacts.summary: The Thanjavur temple is the masterpiece of Chola architecture and a UNESCO World Heritage property. Its plan, sculpture programme and inscriptions form a single interpretable archive.

text.note: Attach the temple inscription record and architectural description.

entries: Link architecture layers to the Brihadeeswarar inscription record.
Use ASI/UNESCO citations for conservation status.

provenance.value: Public heritage metadata; images require per-source rights.

artifacts.summary: The yazh is the harp of Sangam poetry, central to pann music and the imagery of Tamil love and war. No complete ancient instrument survives; reconstructions are interpretive.

value: Sangam poems refer to the yāḻ, its strings, pann and players. Use the corpus search to collect references.

entries: Label every reconstruction as interpretive, not an excavated object.

provenance.value: Reference record; any image must carry the Commons licence.

artifacts.holder: British Library / Tamil Nadu State Archives
artifacts.summary: Colonial maps of Madurai and Tamil towns preserve street layouts, temples, tanks and river courses. They are a bridge between the Sangam city and the modern urban archive.

text.note: Attach a specific map shelfmark and georeferenced transcription.

entries: Do not reuse a map image unless the British Library item is Public Domain Mark.
Reader should support map pan/zoom, place-name index and georeference layer.

provenance.value: Class record; no map image reproduced.

artifacts.summary: Arikamedu was a major bead-making and trade centre. Beads are a compact entry point into craft production, exchange and daily ornament in early Tamil society.

text.note: Object catalogue and excavation context form the text layer.

entries: Record material, shape, drill technique and context.

provenance.value: Excavation metadata; image rights per museum.

artifacts.summary: Black-and-red ware is a diagnostic ceramic of early historic Tamil sites, including Arikamedu. Form and fabric layers connect excavation reports to daily life.

text.note: Attach a specific vessel form and excavation context.

entries: Reader layers should include fabric, form, surface treatment and context.

provenance.value: Public excavation metadata; image rights per museum.

artifacts.summary: Nineteenth-century Tamil printed editions show the transition from palm-leaf to print, including new punctuation, title pages and editorial conventions.

text.note: Attach a public-domain scan and page-level transcription.

entries: Use only public-domain scans, not lending-only copies.
Page-level reader should support facing transcription and modern Tamil gloss.

provenance.value: Class record; no scan attached.
